title: Cornelius' vision (Acts 10:1–33)
hookLine: some guests you plan for. some arrive at the gate while lunch is still cooking
tomorrow: what's the first thing Peter says in a stranger's house?

lines: A HUNGRY MAN ON A ROOF.
cards: Some guests you plan for for weeks. Some knock at the gate while lunch is still on the stove. Today has both, in two cities.
In Caesarea lives a Roman officer, Cornelius, "A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway."

An angel tells him to send to Joppa for a man named Peter, so the soldier sends for the fisherman. The next day in Joppa, Peter goes up on a roof to pray, "And he became very hungry, and would have eaten."

teach.b: While the meal is cooking, Peter sees something like a great sheet let down from heaven, full of all kinds of animals, and hears: "Rise, Peter; kill, and eat."

He refuses: "Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean." He has kept the food laws faithfully, and he says so. The voice answers: "What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common."
Three times, and the sheet goes back up. Peter is still puzzling when the men from Cornelius knock at the gate. He calls them in and gives them a place to stay.
A day later he walks into the house of a Gentile, full of Cornelius' relatives and friends, and tells them what the sheet meant.
It wasn't about lunch: "God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean."
Two visions, two cities, and a door opened from both sides.

how: Some Christians read Peter's rooftop vision as a call to welcome people across lines of nation and custom, and to open the door before every question is answered.

o: Peter's dream of a ladder reaching to heaven
a soldier's vision that sent him looking for Peter
a Roman governor's dream about Jesus' trial

games.q: two visions, two cities — tap the pairs.
p: a centurion who prayed to God alway
where the men from Caesarea knocked

s: Peter's vision was mainly about a new menu
he tells Cornelius' house: God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
Cornelius was already devout before Peter came
he feared God with all his house, gave alms and prayed to God alway.
Peter went to Caesarea the same afternoon
he lodged the men first and set out the next day.

games.q: a new coworker eats different food from everyone and keeps to herself at lunch. what's Peter's move from today?
o: make room for her at your table, and let her eat what she eats.
wait for her to get used to how everyone else eats first.
ask her to explain her food rules before you invite her.
games.why: the sheet was about people: Peter learned not to call any man common or unclean, and called the strangers in before he fully understood.

practice: For the sit, listen for the sounds that reach you from outside: a car, footsteps, a dog, the wind. Don't sort them into welcome and unwelcome.
Let each one arrive and pass, the way Peter heard the knock at the gate and called the strangers in.

wordCard.voice: Cornelius' vision. A Roman centurion is told to send for Peter, while Peter has a vision of his own.

orig.note: Greek: common; Peter's word in Acts 10:14, common or unclean.
